stage1.impression: A dark, warm, brown-red room with a red acrylic speaker glowing at its centre, a record wall on the right and a leather chair in the foreground. It reads as a CG proof, not a photograph: the speaker is half hidden behind a side table and a small lamp, its upper section is a dim translucent box that seems to float, the concrete is a mottled brown smear with no formwork, the record wall is evenly dull with no pools of light, and the big frosted screen reads as a stained grey sheet. There are no visible practicals giving the room its light, so the red glow does the lighting, and the wall around the speaker turns red.

blocking_9: The speaker is unobstructed and read at a glance: no lamp or side table crossing its face, base and top both visible, and the whole cabinet (upper section included) lit to lum_median >= 60
At least two warm practicals visible in frame (Bell, sconce or pendant) making their own pools on surfaces, so the room is not lit by the red speaker
Neutral surfaces stay neutral: the concrete beside the speaker within about 8 of r-b at warm white, not red
The concrete shows board-formed grain, tie holes and pour lines at 1:1; the fir beams are visible overhead with checks and end grain
The record wall has pools of light with falloff (spines legible in the pools, dark between them), not a flat dull field
The frosted screen reads as a thick frosted panel with an image glowing evenly behind it, set in a reveal, not a stained sheet
The leather chair shows real leather: a soft sheen, creases, piping, a highlight from a practical
A sign of life: a glass on the side table, a record out of its sleeve, a coat on the chair
Delivered at full resolution with no denoiser mottle on the walls

defects.what: Bell lamp's stem and the side table sit across the speaker's left edge and horn; the lamp head is a small white blob against the red
side table top cuts the speaker's base; objects on it are dark lumps, not readable glasses
upper section of the speaker is underlit (lum_median 24) and reads as a loose translucent box floating above the lower cabinet
concrete is a mottled red-brown smear (r 36 g 19 b 12), no board marks, tie holes or pour lines; denoiser blotching
screen reads as a flat grey sheet with a dark stain; no thickness, no reveal, no glow from behind; the image does not read as fogged glass or a silhouette
record wall flat and dim (median 19, falloff bins 16 to 23 with no pools); repeated sleeves read as a texture
foreground leather chair is a rough matte red-brown shell, no sheen, seams or creases; reads as plastic or felt
fir beam barely legible at the top edge; ceiling falls into mud
no visible warm practical anywhere apart from the lamp head; the light has no source

changes.problem: The hero speaker is blocked by the Bell lamp and the side table, so its silhouette, horn and base cannot be read.

evidence.measured: lamp stem and head cross x 250-285; table top covers y 400-480 of the cabinet; speaker region lum_median 47.7, only just at the 45 floor

change.setting: props / side table and Bell placement
change.from: table and Bell directly between camera and the speaker's left half
change.to: move the side table about 0.6 m toward the chair (camera left) so it sits beside the speaker, not in front; Bell on that table, its head clear of the cabinet's outline; put a rocks glass and a record out of its sleeve on the table

changes.expected: the whole speaker outline, horn and base visible; Bell becomes a visible warm practical beside it

changes.problem: The speaker's upper section is underlit and the cabinet as a whole is too dim to be the hero.

evidence.measured: lum_median 24.0, lum_range 16.8, against 47.7 for the lower cabinet

change.setting: lamps on each Ember speaker (4 x area)
change.to: 20 W/m2, with one of the four aimed at the upper section; keep 2900 K

changes.expected: upper section reads as part of the same cabinet; the light passing through the red acrylic is legible top to bottom

changes.problem: The room has no warm practical lighting it, so the red speaker's spill lights the concrete and the walls turn red instead of warm grey.

evidence.measured: concrete r_median 36, g 19, b 12, lum_median 22.4; no pools

change.setting: sconces 1 x point and Bell 6 lamps
change.from: sconce 20 W 2400 K; Bell 18 W each
change.to: sconce 45 W at 2700 K placed on the concrete pier between the screen and the speaker so it grazes the wall; Bell 30 W at 2700 K

changes.expected: a pool of warm light grazing the concrete, which reads warm grey rather than red; the red becomes local to the speaker

changes.problem: The record wall is lit evenly and dully, with no pools of light and no legible spines.

evidence.measured: lum_median 19.3, falloff bins 16.3 to 22.9 along y with no peak

change.to: 25 W, 18 deg, 2700 K, aimed at three separate bays; strip 0.1

changes.expected: three distinct pools with spines legible inside them, dark between

changes.problem: The concrete reads as a mottled smear with no formwork grain, tie holes or pour lines.

evidence.measured: 3x crop shows only blotchy noise; lum_range 17

change.to: lighter warm grey (base albedo about 0.35), a faint satin sheen (roughness about 0.7) so grazing light picks out board grain at 140 mm board width, tie holes on a 600 mm grid and a pour line

changes.expected: board grain and tie holes legible at 1:1 where the sconce grazes the wall

changes.problem: The screen reads as a stained sheet, not a thick frosted panel with an image glowing behind it.

evidence.measured: lum_median 28, lum_range 28.5, flat grey; no edge glow or reveal

change.setting: screens' images and frosted acrylic roughness
change.to: image 0.5 with a darker field so the figure glows rather than the sheet; frost roughness up so the image blurs softly; light the panel's polished edge so the 30 mm thickness shows

changes.expected: panel reads as frosted acrylic with a soft suggestive image behind it, dimmer field, glowing edge

changes.problem: The leather chair reads as a rough matte plastic shell.

change.setting: leather finish and a coat prop
change.to: dark tan leather with roughness about 0.45 and a creased normal map, piping on the edges; drape a coat over the arm

changes.expected: a soft highlight on the chair's shoulder from Bell; leather reads at 1:1

changes.problem: At 24 mm from close range the speaker is small and the frame is dominated by dim wall; the beams overhead are lost.

evidence.measured: speaker occupies about 16 percent of frame width

change.to: 35 mm, stepped back about 0.8 m along x and raised to 1.2 m, tilted only by shift, so the speaker fills about a quarter of the frame width and a beam crosses the top edge

changes.expected: speaker reads as the hero; a fir beam with end grain visible at the top; verticals true

out_of_scope.request: Separate the speaker's upper and lower sections visually so the top does not read as a floating box
out_of_scope.why: the speaker's shape and parts are fixed; only its light (c2) can change

out_of_scope.request: Make the record wall less repetitive with varied shelf heights
out_of_scope.why: the record wall's design is fixed; vary the sleeves (props) instead if possible
